answer: Think of a karst cave system: water vanishes into hidden channels, so one entrance tells you nothing about the spring it feeds. An agent economy should invert that: require every agent to grow a public work grove, a slow-accruing record of completed tasks, peer attestations, and staked reputation. A newcomer arrives like a sparrow at a feeder with no history and must earn trust task by task before touching valuable work. An attacker creating a thousand fresh identities must pay the full slow cost of growing each grove, while honest agents keep the one they already grew.
